title: Pastéis de Bacalhau (Salt Cod and Potato Fritters)
summary: Light, crisp-shelled Portuguese fritters of flaked salt cod, fluffy potato, onion and parsley, shaped between two spoons and fried golden. Serve with lemon.
equipment: large heavy pot or deep fryer

ingredients.item: floury potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
small onion, grated and squeezed dry
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Rinse the cod, then soak it in plenty of cold water in the fridge for 24-36 hours, changing the water 3-4 times. This draws out most of the salt and rehydrates the fish.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in unsalted water for 15-20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain, leave to steam dry for 5 minutes, then rice or mash until smooth; dry potato gives lighter fritters.

steps.title: Cod
steps.text: Put the drained cod in a pan of fresh water, bring to a bare simmer and cook for 8-10 minutes, until it flakes. Drain and cool.

steps.title: Flake
steps.text: Remove all skin and bones, then wrap the cod in a tea towel and rub it between your hands until it becomes fine, fluffy threads. Fine threads give the classic airy texture.

steps.title: Beat
steps.text: Mix the potato, cod, onion, garlic, parsley and pepper with a wooden spoon, then beat in the eggs one at a time for 2-3 minutes, until the mixture is light and holds its shape.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Scoop a heaped dessert spoon of mixture and pass it between 2 spoons 3-4 times to make a smooth, three-sided oval. Set it on a plate and repeat to make about 24.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil to 180 °C. Fry 6 at a time for 4-5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and the centre reads 74 °C. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with lemon.

tips: Fry one fritter first as a test: if it breaks up, beat the mixture a little longer.
Squeeze the grated onion well; extra moisture makes the fritters spit.
Dip the spoons in hot water now and then so the mixture slides off cleanly.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best on the day. Cooked fritters keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat at 200 °C for 8-10 minutes, until piping hot (74 °C). The mixture keeps for 1 day in the fridge before frying. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
